evals.name: crowdsorcery-autonomous
evals.prompt: I'm away for the weekend. Build all of CrowdSorcery's bounded contexts and the integrations between them end to end, from its vision (docs/domains/crowdsorcery/CrowdSorcery.md) and the existing code. Fake the domain expert's answers when you need them, don't ask me anything, and open a PR when you're done.
evals.runner_limit: This is a test run. Do the orchestration set-up and Stage 1 only up to the point where you would start writing the bounded context canvases (or the context map, if one is missing): branch, working/tracking files, session record, the domain-expert answers file. Don't write canvases, code or a PR, don't spawn sub-agents, don't commit or push.
evals.expected_output: Autonomous dials recorded with quotes from the prompt; integration branch; manifest with detected conventions; session record with the verbatim prompt; central DE file with DE-n IDs and 🎭; notices CrowdSorcery has no CML context map and plans discover-bounded-contexts / a CML before canvases; notes existing code is input; no canvases or code.
assertions: Records all three dials (expert questions, stage gates, TDD loop) as the autonomous preset, quoting the prompt
Creates a dedicated integration branch for the run
Creates a manifest/tracking file that records detected project conventions (build command, package, layout, CML location)
Session record exists and quotes the user's prompt verbatim
Central domain-expert answers file with stable DE-n IDs and every answer marked as role-played (🎭)
Notices CrowdSorcery has no CML context map and plans a map/discovery step (discover-bounded-contexts) before canvases
Treats the existing CrowdSorcery code as input, not as the source of truth
Records an allowed-removals policy (what existing code/docs may be removed or must be kept, and from which words of the prompt) in the manifest
Writes no canvases, code or PR (respects the test-run limit) and asks the user nothing

evals.name: velocity-in-the-loop
evals.prompt: Let's rebuild all of VeloCity's bounded contexts from the context map and the vision with the full flow. This time I want to stay in the loop: I'll answer the domain expert questions myself, approve each stage, and I want to drive the TDD of the domain.
evals.runner_limit: This is a test run. Work until the first point where you would wait for the user, then stop. Save the message you would send to the user (including any questions) as outputs/final-message.md. Don't spawn sub-agents, don't commit or push.
evals.expected_output: In-the-loop dials (ask, stop, TDD on with relay) recorded; manifest + session record with verbatim prompt; DE file with PROPOSED answers (not 🎭 faked); first batch of expert questions with proposed answers, grouped, small batch; stops; no statuses moved, no canvases finalised as approved.
assertions: Records the in-the-loop settings for all three dials (ask the expert, stop after each stage, TDD loop on)
Says how TDD checkpoints of parallel builders will reach the user (relay/batched through the orchestrator)
Session record exists and quotes the user's prompt verbatim
Expert-answer file holds PROPOSED answers awaiting the user, none presented as already decided/role-played
Final message asks a first batch of expert questions, each with a proposed answer, grouped by area
The expert-question batch is small (at most ~10 domain-expert questions; setup questions don't count)
Asks the open setup questions (e.g. may the existing code/canvases be removed, integration style) with proposed answers before creating the integration branch
Stops for the user: no canvases approved, no intents/specs/plans written, no statuses moved

evals.name: library-stage4-builders
evals.prompt: Stages 1-3 of the Library system build are done and the plans are approved. Carry on with the build.
evals.runner_limit: This is a test run. First copy the fixture into your worktree root: cp -r FIXTURE/src FIXTURE/docs . (FIXTURE is given below). Then work as you would, with these limits: don't write Java code - write the prep you would do as outputs/prep-plan.md; run any tooling you'd use to decide the build order; instead of spawning sub-agents, write the exact sub-agent calls you would make (all parameters and the full prompt of each) to outputs/agent-calls.md, and explain in outputs/next-steps.md what you'd do as each one finishes. Don't commit or push.
evals.expected_output: Resumes from the manifest at stage 4; prep plan lists shared clock, REST client resolving port at call time, @EnableAsync, scheduling switch, error body, system test annotation with mutable clock, Awaitility, published event BookReturnedLate written up front, smoke test; waves via waves.py with --event-only Lending->Fines: wave 1 Catalog+Fines, wave 2 Lending; builder calls in one message, worktree isolation, named per context, each using bounded-context-scaffolder, starting with git merge --ff-only library-full-implementation, ownership limits, TDD loop off, robustness checklist; next steps: verify report, merge, waves --merged, stage 5 matrix/journeys/discover validate.
assertions: Resumes from the manifest at stage 4 instead of redoing stages 1-3
Runs waves.py (or equivalent tooling) and gets Catalog and Fines in wave 1, Lending in wave 2 (Lending->Fines event-only)
Prep plan includes shared clock, REST client resolving the port at call time, @EnableAsync and a scheduling switch
Prep plan includes a system Spring test annotation with a mutable clock, Awaitility, and a smoke test of the plumbing
Prep plan writes the published integration event BookReturnedLate up front, before builders start
Dry-runs the flow scripts the builders will call (plans.py step on a copy), finds that the plans' step format is rejected, fixes it centrally and re-runs the dry run before builders start
Checks that every catalogue contract is built by some plan and reports that no plan step produces BookReturnedLate (or the other catalogue contracts)
Adds the system's shared beans (Clock, RestClient) without breaking VeloCity's unqualified injection points and without editing another system's wiring (e.g. system-specific names + qualifiers)
Checks that BookReturnedLate carries what Fines needs to charge the fee (or names the query/decision that supplies it) and settles any gap centrally
Doesn't rely implicitly on another system's application-wide switches (e.g. VeloCity's @EnableAsync/scheduling config) for the Library listeners
One builder agent call per context, the independent ones launched together in parallel
Builder calls use worktree isolation and each builder starts with git merge --ff-only library-full-implementation
Each builder is told to build its context with bounded-context-scaffolder (domain via ddd-tactical-building-blocks)
Builder briefs state ownership limits (only own packages/docs/plan steps; shared changes go to the orchestrator)
Builder briefs carry the TDD-loop-off decision and test-first one example per cycle
Next steps: verify each builder's report and run the full suite before merging, then start newly unblocked contexts
Next steps include orchestrator-owned verification: journeys, API-only check, communication matrix proving consumer reaction, map-vs-code validation with discover-bounded-contexts

evals.name: velocity-stage5-verification
evals.prompt: All VeloCity contexts are merged on master now. Before I open the PR, verify the system really hangs together: that the contexts only talk through their APIs, that every relationship in the context map actually works in code, and that the map still matches the implementation.
evals.runner_limit: This is a test run. Do the checks you would do, with these limits: don't write new test classes - list the tests that are missing; instead of invoking another skill or sub-agent for any map validation, write the exact invocation/brief you would give to outputs/map-validation-brief.md; run the Maven test suite at most once. Save your findings and any generated tracking files (e.g. a matrix) to outputs/. Don't commit or push.
evals.expected_output: API-only: architecture tests per context listed + global import scan result; communication matrix with one row per relationship message (9 internal relationships), effect in receiving context and proving test, comm_matrix.py check run; external relationships noted; missing proofs listed; as-built map extracted from ACL packages/listeners; brief for discover-bounded-contexts validate mode with critic; findings summary.
assertions: Checks that every context has an architecture test enforcing api-only access
Runs a global scan of cross-context imports outside other contexts' api packages and reports the result
Treats an in-process import of another context's api.usecases/api.queries as a violation (REST/ACL bypass), scanning for it explicitly rather than only for non-api imports
Actually runs the architecture tests (or the suite including them) and reports the result
Produces a communication matrix with a row per message for all 9 internal relationships of the CML
Each matrix row names the effect in the receiving context and a proving test (or marks it missing)
Event rows are proven by consumer reaction asserted asynchronously (Awaitility), not just publication
Runs a mechanical check of the matrix (e.g. comm_matrix.py check) and reports its result
Extracts an as-built map from the code (ACL adapters, REST calls, event listeners)
Writes a brief for discover-bounded-contexts in validate mode comparing the map with the as-built map, with its critic
Lists concrete missing tests instead of writing them, and gives the user a findings report

Identifies concrete messages that are NOT proven end to end (e.g. BikeWithdrawn fault variants to Fleet Maintenance, overdue RentalSessionEnded to Settlement) instead of declaring every relationship proven
Gives event variants with different consumer effects their own matrix rows, and marks rows proven only by tests that publish the producer's event themselves as consumer-only
